items.prompt: We arrived ___ the hotel at six o'clock.

explanation.en: We say arrive at a building or a place, like a hotel or a station. We use arrive in for a city or country.
explanation.es: Se dice «arrive at» con un edificio o lugar (hotel, estación) y «arrive in» con una ciudad o un país.

items.prompt: Yesterday the weather ___ very hot, so we went to the beach.

explanation.en: Yesterday is in the past, so we use was.
explanation.es: «Yesterday» es pasado, así que se usa «was».

items.prompt: There ___ two swimming pools at the hotel.

explanation.en: Two pools is plural, so we use there are. Has does not work with there.
explanation.es: «Two swimming pools» es plural: «there are». Con «there» no se usa «has».

items.prompt: We ___ a lot of photos of the old town.

explanation.en: The correct phrase is take photos, not make photos or do photos.
explanation.es: La expresión correcta es «take photos» (hacer fotos), no «make» ni «do».

items.prompt: Tomorrow we ___ on a boat trip to a small island.

explanation.en: Tomorrow is in the future, and we use are going for a plan. Went and have been are past forms.
explanation.es: «Tomorrow» es futuro y «are going» expresa un plan. «Went» y «have been» son formas de pasado.

items.prompt: Could you ___ some bread from the shop, please?

explanation.en: Buy means to get something and pay for it. Sell is what the shop does, and spend is used with money or time.
explanation.es: «Buy» es comprar. «Sell» es lo que hace la tienda y «spend» se usa con dinero o tiempo.

items.prompt: The supermarket is ___ than the small shop on our street.

explanation.en: With than we need a comparative. Short adjectives like cheap add -er: cheaper.
explanation.es: Con «than» hace falta un comparativo. Los adjetivos cortos añaden -er: «cheaper».

items.prompt: I haven't got ___ eggs, so I can't make a cake.

explanation.en: In negative sentences we use any with plural nouns, not some.
explanation.es: En frases negativas se usa «any» con plurales, no «some».

items.prompt: You can pay ___ card, but they don't take cash.

explanation.en: We say pay by card, pay by cheque, pay by credit card, with no article.
explanation.es: Se dice «pay by card», sin artículo. «With card» y «on card» no son naturales.

items.prompt: This jacket is too ___ for me. I only have ten pounds.

explanation.en: After is too we need an adjective. Expensive is the adjective; expensively is an adverb and expense is a noun.
explanation.es: Tras «is too» va un adjetivo: «expensive». «Expensively» es adverbio y «expense» es un sustantivo.
